title: Telecom SOP §1.1 — Core Optical Transport & DWDM Fiber Switch (Resource Type 1)
trigger: resource_type 1 alerts or optical loss warnings
description: Operating procedure for optical transport switch degradation, laser drift, or chromatic dispersion on Resource Type 1.
standard_operating_procedure: Check Bit Error Rate (BER) counters and optical power levels on ingress and egress transponders.
Verify DWDM wavelength alignment and optical amplifier gain tilt.
If optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) drops below 18dB, switch traffic to protection fiber path.

title: Telecom SOP §1.2 — Edge BGP / MPLS Provider Edge Router (Resource Type 2)
trigger: resource_type 2 alerts, route flaps, or multi-event routing storms
description: Troubleshooting protocol for MPLS provider edge router interface flaps, routing loops, and session resets on Resource Type 2.
standard_operating_procedure: Inspect BGP session state, keepalive timer intervals, and prefix limit drops.
Verify MTU configuration consistency across adjacent peer interfaces.
If multipath failover storms (Event 42, 43, 44) occur, pin traffic to primary MPLS tunnel and damp flapping routes.

title: Telecom SOP §1.3 — Microwave Wireless Backhaul Transceiver (Resource Type 3)
trigger: resource_type 3 alerts, rain fade, or dish alignment drift
description: Resolution procedure for wireless backhaul signal attenuation, RSSI degradation, or adaptive modulation drops on Resource Type 3.
standard_operating_procedure: Check Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) against baseline link budget.
Enable adaptive coding and modulation (ACM) to maintain link stability under adverse atmospheric conditions.
Inspect antenna physical alignment and coaxial waveguide integrity if degradation persists.

title: Telecom SOP §1.4 — High-Density Switching Fabric Card (Resource Type 4)
trigger: resource_type 4 alerts, ASIC parity errors, or fabric buffer exhaustion
description: Emergency remediation protocol for switching fabric packet drops, buffer overflow, and backplane bus contention on Resource Type 4.
standard_operating_procedure: Inspect egress buffer queue depth and packet discard counters across fabric ASICs.
Initiate graceful fabric plane rebalancing to offload congested switching slices.
If parity error detected, trigger diagnostic self-test and schedule module replacement.

title: Telecom SOP §1.5 — Substation Power Distribution Unit & UPS (Resource Type 5)
trigger: resource_type 5 alerts, voltage sag, or phase imbalance
description: Safety and electrical remediation for substation PDU, DC rectifier, and battery backup alarms on Resource Type 5.
standard_operating_procedure: Verify -48V DC bus voltage and rectifier load sharing across power shelves.
Check UPS battery discharge state and thermal sensor readings.
Dispatch field electrical team immediately if secondary rectifier feed has tripped.

title: Telecom SOP §1.6 — Cellular Baseband Unit & RAN Controller (Resource Type 6)
trigger: resource_type 6 alerts, CPRI synchronization failure, or radio frame loss
description: Procedures for baseband unit clock loss, CPRI/eCPRI optical interface errors, and sector carrier drops on Resource Type 6.
standard_operating_procedure: Verify GPS / IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol (PTP) synchronization lock.
Check optical transceivers linking BBU to Remote Radio Heads (RRH).
Perform soft reset of digital signal processing (DSP) pool if carrier allocation fails.

title: Telecom SOP §1.7 — Carrier Ethernet Access Node & DSLAM/OLT (Resource Type 7)
trigger: resource_type 7 alerts, broadcast storms, or subscriber port flapping
description: Remediation workflow for last-mile aggregation access nodes, GPON OLT line cards, and MAC address table exhaustion on Resource Type 7.
standard_operating_procedure: Apply broadcast/multicast storm suppression filters on uplink trunk ports.
Verify optical split ratio and subscriber ONT optical power levels.
Clear stagnant MAC learning entries and monitor port status for 10 minutes.

title: Telecom SOP §1.8 — Primary Optical Line Terminal & Fiber Distribution Hub (Resource Type 8)
trigger: resource_type 8 alerts, high optical receiver overload, or core backhaul degradation
description: Critical response protocol for primary optical distribution hub line cards, feeder fiber attenuation, and transceiver faults on Resource Type 8.
standard_operating_procedure: Isolate fiber line transceivers on Resource Type 8 and inspect optical launch power.
Execute automated Optical Time Domain Reflectometer (OTDR) trace to locate physical fiber breaks or high-attenuation bends.
Clean SC/APC optical patch connectors and verify optical link loss budget (<15dB).
If accompanied by log_feature 82 surge or Event 15 reset, initiate immediate field dispatch for line card replacement.

title: Telecom SOP §1.9 — Environmental Site Sensors & HVAC Systems (Resource Type 9)
trigger: resource_type 9 alerts, high temperature, or humidity thresholds
description: Protocol for cabinet thermal excursions, cooling unit failure, and site humidity alarms on Resource Type 9.
standard_operating_procedure: Check cabinet internal temperature probe readings against 35°C threshold.
Activate backup HVAC cooling unit and verify air filter intake clearance.
If temperature exceeds 45°C, initiate graceful traffic shed to prevent thermal equipment shutdown.

title: Telecom SOP §1.10 — Security Gateway & Deep Packet Inspection Appliance (Resource Type 10)
trigger: resource_type 10 alerts, state table exhaustion, or DDoS throttling
description: Incident workflow for security gateway state table saturation, crypto engine bottlenecks, and packet inspection overloads on Resource Type 10.
standard_operating_procedure: Inspect active TCP connection state table utilization against maximum threshold.
Flush expired session timers and engage hardware SYN-cookie defense.
Bypass non-critical deep packet inspection policies to maintain transit line-rate throughput.

title: Telecom SOP §2.1 — Link State Flapping & Loss of Signal (Event Type 11)
description: Standard procedure for physical link loss-of-signal (LOS) alarms and continuous port flapping events.
standard_operating_procedure: Inspect optical power levels and physical seating of SFP+/QSFP transceivers.
Configure link debounce timer (100ms) to prevent rapid route withdrawal storms.
If link fails to stabilize within 5 flap cycles, force failover to redundant standby link.

title: Telecom SOP §2.2 — Critical Module Parity Error & Abrupt Reset (Event Type 15)
description: Emergency protocol for abrupt hardware module reboots, uncorrectable memory parity errors, and kernel panics.
standard_operating_procedure: Capture kernel crash dump logs and line card register states before restart.
Isolate the failing module from the active forwarding plane to prevent split-brain routing.
Schedule urgent on-site technician intervention for physical module swap.

title: Telecom SOP §2.3 — Multipath Route Storm & Convergence Loop (Event Types 42, 43, 44)
description: Resolution procedure for cascading routing protocol convergence loops and multipath failover storms.
standard_operating_procedure: Activate BGP route dampening to penalize persistently flapping peer prefixes.
Force traffic onto deterministic static label-switched paths (LSP).
Inspect upstream transit provider links for wide-area fiber cuts.

title: Telecom SOP §3.1 — High-Volume Framing Error & Buffer Congestion (Log Feature 82)
description: Diagnostics for severe frame check sequence (FCS) errors, buffer overruns, and packet corruption on critical optical interfaces.
standard_operating_procedure: Purge transit buffer queue and inspect port error counters for CRC/FCS increments.
Verify optical signal-to-noise ratio and clean optical fiber connectors.
Cross-reference with Resource Type 8 status to assess line card degradation.

title: Telecom SOP §3.2 — Hardware Interrupt Loop & Queue Starvation (Log Feature 203)
description: Remediation for CPU interrupt storming, driver watchdog timeouts, and telemetry queue starvation.
standard_operating_procedure: Inspect line card CPU utilization and disable verbose debug logging.
Restart the local device telemetry polling agent.
If CPU remains pegged >95%, trigger controlled sub-card reload.
citation: Telecom SOP Manual §3.2 (Interrupt Loops & CPU Watchdogs)

title: Telecom SOP §3.3 — Packet Drop Threshold Exceeded (Log Feature 71)
description: Bandwidth saturation and tail-drop resolution protocol.
standard_operating_procedure: Verify traffic bandwidth against interface link capacity.
Tune Weighted Random Early Detection (WRED) queue profiles.
Re-route non-critical bulk traffic to secondary link.
